overall_assessment.realism: The samples are highly realistic, reflecting common spear phishing tactics such as domain impersonation, use of recently registered domains with privacy protection, spoofed email headers, and targeted social engineering content. The technical details like email headers, SMTP logs, domain registration info, and phishing URL analyses are detailed and plausible. The inclusion of phishing scores, detection methods, and relevant MITRE ATT&CK techniques further enhances authenticity. The scenarios cover diverse attack vectors including credential harvesting via fake portals, malicious macro attachments, and embedded keyloggers, which are typical in real-world campaigns.
overall_assessment.consistency: The dataset is consistent in structure and schema across all samples. Each entry contains the required fields: scenario, technical_data (with email headers, body, SMTP logs, domain registration, phishing URL or null), indicators, detection_method, and relevant_mitre_techniques. The formatting of email headers and SMTP logs is uniform. Domain registration and phishing URL details are consistently presented with similar subfields. Indicators and detection methods are well aligned with the scenario and technical data. Minor variations such as null phishing_url in attachment-based samples are appropriate and handled correctly.
suggestions: Include explicit attachment metadata (e.g., filename, hash, file size) in the technical_data for samples with malicious attachments to improve clarity and support automated analysis.
Add timestamps or date fields for email receipt and detection events to enhance temporal context.
Standardize the representation of IP addresses by including both IPv4 and IPv6 where applicable to reflect modern network environments.
In phishing_url.url_analysis, consider adding automated risk scores or reputation data to complement qualitative descriptions.
For scenarios involving embedded scripts or macros, include sample code snippets or indicators of compromise to enrich technical detail.
Clarify the relationship between X-Originating-IP and SMTP originating IP when they differ, to avoid confusion.
Consider adding a field for user response or outcome (e.g., whether credentials were compromised) to provide end-to-end attack lifecycle context.
